title: Buddy Petit's odd chords versus Chris Kelly's plunger style
summary: Buddy played slow pieces with odd chords, unlike Chris Kelly who played straight with a plunger; Bunk Johnson-style cigarette paper pads mentioned.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, Punchy just told us that they never did use Flight of Fist around here.

Until that bebop business came out then. That's right. But yet I listen to some of those old Red Island records from 29 or so, and you hear him doing some of those funny changes. Mm-hmm. Yeah. So I wonder, maybe he picked that up in New York. But Buddy never did that kind of stuff, huh? Buddy Petitti ever.

Buddy didn't play fast as we were down here. But Buddy used to play slow pieces and make all kinds of funny chords in them. That's the truth. If he played in B flat, he'd come up with some kind of, B flat on his trumpet, he'd come up with some kind of A flat, B natural, C sharp, and E natural. Look, them all kinds of funny chords, you know. All that was funny stuff, you know.
How did it sound? It sounded good.

Do-do-do-do-dee, bo-do-do-dee, you know what I mean, Paul. Like that, all that kind of stuff. You could do that. Would Chris run those chords? No, Chris played most with a plunger. Yeah. And he played- He played straight along, but he played with a plunger.
Yeah. He'd play ordinary chords, just fifths and ordinary seventh blues chords and stuff like that, but not much money.
But Buddy used to make some funny stuff, man. Oh, God. That's very interesting. We're talking about Buddy.
Buddy Petit. Yeah. I say he used to make some peculiar chords, didn't he?

Oh, yeah. Yeah. He's like Cindy Bessier, you know. He used to make the chords, Paul Woodman, ain't he? He said he couldn't like the music that Cindy Bessier made. John Rovershoe said that too. Yeah. And he used to play an old broken chord, get the melody out of it. Pack it up with paper like this, cigarette paper, his pads, you know. Did you work with, uh, you know, a little bit of a melody out of it? Mm-hm. Did you work with, uh, Be Cher much? and get the melody out of it. Pack it up with paper like this, cigarette paper, it's bad, you know.
